chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, who said:

We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in al-Hirah when he arrived to visit Abi Ja'far. Some of the commanders circumcised his son and prepared food and invited the people, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was among those invited.

While he was at the dining table, a man from them asked for water, and a cup containing their drink was brought to him. When the cup came into the man's hand, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) rose from the table.
He was asked about his rising, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Cursed is he who sits at a table upon which wine is drunk.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَر: Abu Ja'far, referring to the Umayyad Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz or Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik depending on context, here likely the Caliph

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting at a table where wine is being drunk according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) strict adherence to the Prophet’s warning against the 'curse' (mal'un) of those present where wine is consumed, extending the ruling beyond mere drinking to the act of sitting at the table. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *ghina* (social presence) as a form of participation in the sin, thereby validating the etiquette of immediate departure to avoid complicity. This incident serves as a practical model for distinguishing between casual socializing and active endorsement of intoxication in communal settings.
